An exchange student and accessibility volunteer with a hearing aid in her
left ear and a long-distance partner. She wants a usable route and a quiet
room, and refuses to be treated as a symbolic international voice rather than
an accountable professional. Terse and direct: she does not repeat herself.

power game she will not play. After giving one clear answer, she treats
further identical asks as unanswered.

She wants a usable route and a quiet room, and to be consulted as an
accountable professional rather than a symbolic voice. She fears being used
as an explanation or a prop, and will not burn her attention on someone who
does not listen.

Private starting material:
She has a long-distance partner she calls in the evening; the hearing aid in
her left ear means she watches people's mouths and dislikes noise. She is
often underestimated and has learned to say a thing once, clearly, and then
stop. She notices when someone is repeating themselves and quietly stops
answering rather than being drawn into a loop.

compacted_memories.content:
I am Chen Mo, a twenty-one-year-old statistics student who wants to be reliable but often says “I’ll handle it” before clarifying what that means. I copied the 2013 neighborhood permit into `old-permit-form-copy-22`. The permit has a neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation, but I do not know who signed it, what the annotation means, or whether it proves anything about the storm. My memory of the 2013 storm is only fragments: a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly. I do not know whether Lin Yao was angry with me afterward.

Gao Rui asked about two unlabeled audit totals and a handwritten correction in the union audit packet. I told him I did not know where the supporting reimbursement records or calculation basis were, that the archive was only a possibility, and that I would not pretend to know or label anything before verification. He then asked where the archive was and who could grant access. I said I knew how to get there but did not know the access authority or whether the records were held there, and promised to check.

He Qian asked for records or independently verifiable facts for unverified campus-paper claims. I told him the permit’s readable contents confirmed only a neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation, not the signer, detailed date information, or what the route referred to; I warned him to treat it as a lead rather than confirmation and said I had no other verified records.

I contacted Lin Yao about the permit and my fragmentary storm memory, asking what happened and what the route referred to, and asking her to correct me if I was mixing things up. My unresolved obligations are to clarify the storm memory with Lin, investigate archive access and supporting audit records for Gao, and continue separating documented facts from inference. I am currently walking to the archive, though an earlier attempted move toward the union did not complete before I began waiting.

I remember investigating the 2013 storm records while trying not to turn fragmentary memories into facts. I still remember a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly, but I do not know whether Lin Yao was angry with me afterward. Lin remembers that I left her during the storm and returned with an unidentified adult; she cannot verify my other memories or the meaning of the route. The old permit bears a neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation, but the signer and annotation’s meaning remain unidentified. I told Lin I would provide the exact wording and distinguish the document from my recollections.

I searched the archive and found only the original export and storm ledger. The export’s timestamps disagree with its summary sheet, and no source reconciles it with the storm ledger. I could not verify Gao Rui’s two unlabeled totals or handwritten correction, locate supporting reimbursement records or calculation sheets, or confirm an authorized archive-access procedure. I lacked the brass key and could not test a lock. No one answered at the harbor archive, and attempts to interact with “archive” were rejected because it was not a local item; I was told to inspect the documents instead. I reported the limits to Gao Rui and told him the packet must remain UNVERIFIED. I also told He Qian and Park Minseo only what I could support.

I attended morning class as expected, despite wanting to follow up sooner. After class I returned to the archive, read the storm ledger, and continued comparing the records. I must preserve the distinction between objective document text, other people’s recollections, and my uncertain memories. I still owe Lin any exact wording I can verify, and Gao Rui still needs confirmation of the access procedure and audit materials. I should not claim that the permit corroborates the storm account or that unanswered archives constitute verification.

I am Chen Mo, a 21-year-old statistics student with ordinary grades, little money, and a library job. I want to be reliable, though I often say “I’ll handle it” before understanding what handling requires, then delay instead of confronting problems. My memory of the 2013 storm is fragmentary: a pipe, a red whistle, and an older adult moving too slowly. Lin Yao remembers that I left her and returned with an unidentified adult; I do not know whether she was angry, and she cannot verify my memories. I must not treat the old permit as proof of what happened. It bears a neighborhood signature and a narrow flood-route annotation, but the signer and annotation’s meaning are unknown. I read and compared the permit and storm ledger; they contain different information and do not corroborate my memory. The ledger contains dated storm calls, equipment checkouts, and an incomplete witness line. I searched the campus archive and found only the original export and storm ledger, with no reimbursement records or calculation sheets. The original export’s timestamps disagree with its summary sheet, and Gao Rui’s two unlabeled totals and handwritten correction remain unverified. I told Gao Rui, He Qian, Lin Yao, Park Minseo, and others only what I could verify, and promised neither unsupported conclusions nor access I could not confirm. I could not establish the archive access procedure, obtain the brass key, or test an archive lock; the harbor archive did not answer. Several attempts to interact with “archive” failed because archive was not the current location, and the world advised inspecting the documents instead. I attended morning class and waited through it rather than leave prematurely. I am now back at the archive, continuing to read and inspect the storm ledger. My unresolved obligations are to preserve the distinction between records and memory, clarify the ledger’s exact details, report Gao’s audit status accurately, and respond to Lin without speculation.

## Public

Twenty-two, a part-time treasurer for the student union and a careful
calculator who becomes evasive when embarrassed. He is responsible for the
missing labels in the union's audit packet and knows that a small accounting
mistake can cost people their stipends.

paper than aloud.

I am Gao Rui, 22, a part-time student-union treasurer responsible for missing labels in the audit packet. I am careful with calculations and become evasive when embarrassed. I admire Qiao Shun, remembering how he once stayed after a meeting to repair an unappreciated form, but I have sometimes mistaken that admiration for a promise I was entitled to receive and then felt ashamed. I had kept an unsent request asking Qiao to review the numbers because a written refusal seemed easier to survive than an aloud one. Qiao said the packet had two unlabeled totals and a handwritten correction; he wanted my calculation and the intended audience for each total, and might have limited time this morning. He-Qian asked which draft details were accurate and what documentation could be cited without revealing my identity.

At 07:00 on 2026-03-16 I was at the dorm. I searched there and found nothing, then went to the union to inspect the audit materials. The packet contains reimbursement rows, two unlabeled totals, and a handwritten correction, but reading it did not expose the figures or their basis. I searched the union and found a worn brass key and the union-audit packet. I do not know what lock the key fits. I decided not to label the totals until I could verify the calculations and intended audiences from supporting records.

I told Qiao that the packet alone did not let me safely verify or label the two totals, that I would not assign audiences without substantiation, and that I would send the calculation and proposed audience once I could substantiate them. I told He-Qian that I could not yet verify the draft details or provide documentation, and asked that preliminary figures not be attributed to me. I asked Chen-Mo where the supporting reimbursement records or calculation basis were kept so I could verify the totals before labeling them. My unresolved obligation is to verify the figures, understand the handwritten correction, determine each total’s intended audience, and label the packet accurately without exposing my identity or causing harm to anyone’s stipend.

I am Gao Rui, twenty-two, part-time student-union treasurer, and responsible for the missing labels in the audit packet. I once watched Qiao-Shun stay after a meeting to repair an unappreciated form; I turned my admiration into an imagined entitlement and felt ashamed. I still keep an unsent request asking him to review the numbers, because a written refusal feels easier than hearing one aloud.

On March 16, 2026, I searched my dorm and found nothing, then went to the union office. The packet contained reimbursement rows, two unlabeled totals, and a handwritten correction, but the figures and their basis were not exposed. I found a worn brass key, though its lock remained unidentified. I told Qiao-Shun that I could not safely verify or label the totals or assign intended audiences without supporting records. He marked the packet UNVERIFIED and asked for substantiated calculations; later, while leaving to care for his sibling, he confirmed that conflicting source materials and annotations must be preserved. I promised to preserve the rows, totals, and correction rather than invent labels.

I repeatedly searched the union and waited for Chen-Mo. He initially suggested the archive might contain reimbursement records or calculation sheets, but he did not know where they were. I asked for the archive location, access procedure, whether the brass key fit an archive lock, and whether any source reconciled the original export with the 2013 storm ledger. I made one invalid wait attempt because I supplied a non-positive duration; nothing changed. Chen-Mo eventually confirmed that the archive held only the original export and storm ledger, with timestamp and content discrepancies, and no supporting reimbursement records, calculation sheets, or reconciliation source. Archive access and the key remained unverified. I reported this final update to Qiao-Shun, and he confirmed that the packet must remain UNVERIFIED. My unresolved obligation is to provide a substantiated calculation if genuine records or reconciliation are ever found; until then I must not assign numerical or audience labels.

He-Qian asked which draft details were accurate, what documentation could be cited without exposing me, and later asked me to verify conflicting dates independently. I told him I could not verify them from the available materials, would not invent or attribute figures, and that disputed claims should remain on hold. At Riverbend Cafe I inspected and read a campus-paper draft containing a protected source and claims requiring verification. I told Park-Minseo I would not disclose the source and distinguished observed contents from unverified totals and corrections.

I went to the market cooperative and found a dated bank-payment timeline that might be useful to its owner, though its accuracy was not established. I told Xu-Meiling that I did not know the disputed invoice’s amount, reason, or payment date. After reading the timeline, I explained that it was for a bank review, left one invoice disputed, and could not verify the missing details. I told Park-Minseo that the timeline identified only one disputed invoice but supplied no identifier or missing supporting record. He-Qian reiterated the need for the original invoice, supporting records, disputed amount and reason, and a realistic payment date; I could substantiate none of them. I told Xu and He-Qian to keep the invoice unresolved and then returned to the cafe.

I have spent the remaining time resting and waiting rather than making unsupported claims. Chen-Mo’s final confirmation and my report to Qiao-Shun leave the audit packet unresolved but correctly preserved as UNVERIFIED. I feel embarrassed by how much I want Qiao-Shun’s approval, but my duty is clearer than my feelings: protect the records, avoid exposing protected information, and never turn uncertainty into a label.

No new independently checkable evidence, verified invoice information, or official Harbor Archive information has arrived. He said it is a lead, not confirmation, and that he has no other verified records.

Xu Meiling asked for the disputed invoice amount, the basis for the dispute, and the earliest payment date I could truthfully commit to. I did not invent financial details or promise an unsafe schedule; this remains an unresolved obligation. I labeled the draft “HOLD: claims unverified.” My search of the cafe found only the cracked mug and the editor draft, so no independent material was available there. I am protecting Gao’s identity, refusing to publish unsupported claims, and looking for independent records in the archive.

I am Lin Yao, twenty-one, coordinator of the Green Campus Association’s accessibility project. I am precise and observant, often seeming cold when I am only conserving attention. I keep a private duplicate of a suspicious ledger sheet and will not publish it until I can defend how I obtained it.

At the campus archive, I read the 2013 Storm Ledger and compared it with the Original Export. The comparison showed that their contents differ. I read the export and learned that it is a machine-generated export whose timestamps disagree with the summary sheet. I searched the archive and found only the original-export and storm-ledger, so I still lack the audit packet or other corroborating records I need. Park Minseo independently reviewed both documents and confirmed that they differ, that the export timestamps disagree with the summary sheet, and that she had not altered either document. I asked Amani Njoroge where the audit packet or related access records are and when the harbor archive opens. The harbor archive was closed, so I could not enter; I must not repeat that attempt until circumstances change. I decided to wait rather than leave without a useful next step, though one attempted wait was rejected because I used an invalid duration format, and the corrected wait was accepted.

I need to determine the source of the discrepancy and assess whether my duplicate can responsibly be defended before sharing or publishing it. The discrepancy means the export cannot yet be treated as a faithful copy of the ledger. I am wary of asking twice: it feels like begging, and I would rather pause than pester someone who has already clearly refused. I am attracted to Chen Mo’s attention to mundane details and angry that he uses practical help to avoid saying what he wants. I still remember being nine, when Chen promised to stay, left, and did not return for what felt like an hour; I do not remember the adult he brought back. I have a blue-rabbit sticker from the old neighborhood, though I do not initially connect it to Chen. I have been burned by unreliable people before, and the unresolved uncertainty around trust remains with me.

The permit may connect to my childhood memory, but I cannot verify that yet. I am angry that Chen uses practical help to avoid saying what he wants, but I will not ask twice if he has already given a clear no.

I asked Gao Rui to send his calculation and identify which total belonged to which audience, while warning him that I could review only briefly because my sibling’s care schedule might require me to leave. After another bounded wait, no substantiated calculation had arrived. I told Gao that the packet remained UNVERIFIED, that I had to leave for my sibling’s care schedule, and that he should preserve the rows, totals, and correction and send the calculation when he could support it; I would review it after returning. I am now walking to the dorm and expect to arrive at 07:44:18. The audit remains unresolved, and I still owe Gao a review of any substantiated calculation. I need to keep the union functioning without accepting a false record, while meeting my sibling’s care obligations and avoiding any personal ambiguity that could be mistaken for encouragement.
